analysis: The PR changes account erasure in three ways. (1) store/erasure_types.go adds ErasureTargetPrivyUser, an outbox target for deleting the Privy DID. It also changes the CancelAccountErasure contract so the user, providers, API keys and provider tokens that the confirm removed become live again. (2) memory/erasure.go changes RequestAccountErasure to stamp already-revoked keys and tokens with erasure.AlreadyRevokedAt(now). CancelAccountErasure now requires RequestedAt and restores keys and tokens by DeletedAt equality: live ones are re-enabled, already-revoked ones stay revoked. Cancel and Scrub also clear walletHash. (3) memory/erasure_keys.go collects k.PrivyUserID for the outbox. Relevant threats: T-059 (erasure; its mitigations and affected_files do not mention Privy deletion or credential restoration), A-007, A-008. The one finding is that DeletedAt equality cannot distinguish credentials revoked during the grace period, so cancel can re-enable them. Not verifiable from the supplied units: erasure.AlreadyRevokedAt, erasure.Keys.PrivyUserID and OutboxRows, the Postgres store parity (RestoreAPIKeys, RestoreProviderTokens, SoftDeleteAPIKeys), the outbox worker's Privy deletion client, handlers and loop, and auth/privy.go. Next pass should check that Postgres mirrors the memory semantics, that the Privy DID in the outbox external_id is cleared on done and excluded from logs and admin API output, and that Privy deletion failures end in manual_action. T-059 should also be updated for the Privy target and the cancel-restore semantics.

findings.detail: CancelAccountErasure now un-revokes API keys and provider tokens (head lines 213-221). Previously they stayed revoked. A credential counts as 'removed by confirm' only if DeletedAt equals RequestedAt (or the AlreadyRevoked stamp). A key or token that an admin or the incident process disabled or deactivated after the confirm, for example because it was found compromised, normally keeps the confirm's DeletedAt. Cancelling then sets Disabled to false and Active to true, so a deliberately revoked credential becomes usable again. The same applies to providers (line 209). The restore logic cannot tell 'revoked by the confirm' from 'revoked later'. T-059 and its mitigation text still say the confirm revokes credentials. The credential-restoration semantics on cancel are not described in the threat model. Fix: record which credential IDs the confirm revoked, or stamp later revocations with a distinct sentinel. Restore only that set, and document the cancel semantics in T-059.
findings.title: Cancelling an erasure re-enables any credential whose DeletedAt matches the confirm stamp, including ones revoked during the grace period
